comment: Values approximate; verify against NASA sources.
notes: Code generated with AI assistance (Claude). Reviewed by team. Each reference rocket carries a complete 'design' in the real-unit format RocketEvaluator takes (metres, kg, newtons, seconds). Segments stack from the nose tip down: [escape tower] > nose > payload > stages (last stage on top) > fins on the first stage. 'stages' are listed in firing order (index 0 = first stage, at the bottom). Medium mode: slider 0.5 = these values, 0 and 1 = min_factor and max_factor times them. 'real_flight' is the real mission record the launch sim is validated against. 'optional_upper_stage' is the Medium/Hard upper stage at slider 0.5. It is off by default and added with DesignBuilder.add_upper_stage(). It takes the first stage's diameter, and its tank length is computed from the propellant volume unless length_m is set.

reference_rockets.name: Redstone-class
reference_rockets.description: A single-stage alcohol/LOX rocket carrying a small crewed capsule on a suborbital hop.

geometry_notes.overall: Real Mercury-Redstone: about 25.4 m tall including capsule and escape tower, 1.78 m (70 in) diameter, about 30,000 kg (66,000 lb) at liftoff. Here: tower 4.5 + capsule 2.9 + booster 18.0 = 25.4 m; liftoff mass 29,900 kg.
geometry_notes.nose: The capsule itself is the nose. Modelled as a 2.9 m cone weighing 1,300 kg (real capsule about 1,300 kg at launch; it was a blunt truncated cone, not a pointed one).
geometry_notes.payload: The adapter plus instrument compartment between capsule and tanks. Length and mass are ESTIMATES.
geometry_notes.body: Tank section. 12.0 m length is an ESTIMATE (18.0 m booster minus the instrument and tail sections). Propellant 23,600 kg is DERIVED from 350 kN / (215 s x g0) = 166 kg/s times the real 142 s burn. Dry mass 3,000 kg is an ESTIMATE chosen so total liftoff mass matches about 30 t.
geometry_notes.engine: Same numbers as engines.json 'redstone_class' (inspired by the Rocketdyne A-7: 78,000 lbf sea-level thrust). Tail section length 3.5 m is an ESTIMATE.
geometry_notes.fins: Count 4 is real. Span 1.07 m per fin is DERIVED from a roughly 3.9 m overall fin span. Root chord, tip chord, sweep and mass are ESTIMATES from drawings, not sourced numbers.
geometry_notes.options: The real Redstone steered with carbon jet vanes in the exhaust plus air rudders, not a gimbal; 'gimballed: true' stands in for that active steering. Escape tower mass and length are ESTIMATES. The tower's aerodynamics are ignored; only its mass counts.

real_flight.notes: Apogee, range, speed and duration are from memory of the NASA MR-3 mission summary: VERIFY. max_q_pa (about 575 lb/ft2) is LOW CONFIDENCE and may be wrong. Mercury-Redstone 4 (21 July 1961) reached about 190 km and 486 km downrange.

reference_rockets.source: Inspired by the real Mercury-Redstone Launch Vehicle (NASA MSFC, 1960-61). See 'The Mercury-Redstone Project' (NASA TMX-53107, 1964) and 'This New Ocean' (NASA SP-4201) for the numbers to verify against.

optional_upper_stage.source: MADE UP: same as the presets.json 'big' upper stage. The real Mercury-Redstone had no upper stage; the Redstone-derived Jupiter-C / Juno I carried small solid-rocket upper stages instead.

reference_rockets.name: Juno-class
reference_rockets.description: A stretched Redstone-class booster with a stack of small solid-rocket upper stages: an orbital launcher for a small satellite, the way Juno I put Explorer 1 into orbit.

geometry_notes.overall: Real Juno I / Jupiter-C: a Redstone with stretched tanks (about 17 m) carrying a spinning tub of clustered Sergeant solid rockets. Here: booster 19.5 m + two solid stages + payload and nose.
geometry_notes.body: ALL MADE UP / ESTIMATED: tank length 16 m, propellant 24,000 kg and dry mass 3,300 kg are tuned so the reference just reaches the Level 1 orbit (about 2 stars).
geometry_notes.engine: Redstone-class engine with a MADE UP uprate (380 kN sea level): the real Jupiter-C used a slightly uprated Rocketdyne A-7 on a stretched airframe.
geometry_notes.upper_stages: MADE UP. The real tub held 11 + 3 + 1 small solids. Two stacked solid stages stand in for it.

real_flight.notes: From memory: VERIFY. Explorer 1 weighed about 14 kg and reached roughly 358 x 2,550 km.

reference_rockets.source: Inspired by the real Juno I / Jupiter-C launch vehicle (Army Ballistic Missile Agency, 1956-58). Every number here is an estimate or made up for gameplay: see geometry_notes.

optional_upper_stages.source: MADE UP solid-rocket stage (no engine id: values inline). Isp 235 s is typical of 1950s solid propellant (Sergeant-class); everything else is a gameplay estimate.
MADE UP small solid-rocket stage. The real top stage was a single small Sergeant carrying Explorer 1.
